lesson.grammar_point: relative clauses with who, which, that and where to describe people, things and places

listenings.text: Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to Berlin. Passengers who arrived on the flight from Frankfurt, please collect your bags at baggage claim, belt number four. If a bag is missing, please go to the lost luggage office, which is next to belt six. Passengers who have a connecting flight, please follow the signs for transfers. Do not leave the security area. And for passengers who need a taxi to the city, the taxi stand is outside exit B, on the right. Trains and buses that go to the city center leave from the lower level. Thank you, and enjoy your stay in Berlin.

Hi, it's Giulia again. I go to Berlin every year for design events, so here are my tips. First, the neighborhood that I like most is Kreuzberg. It has small restaurants, cafes, and many designers live there. Second, money. Most places take cards, but some small places only take cash, so always have some euros. Third, the trains. The tickets that you buy in the app are easier than the machines. And finally, the food. If it's a cold night, the best local dish is a hot currywurst from a street stand. The people who work there are fast, so know what you want before you get to the front of the line.
